thread:
Ana: Flagging a customer incident that revealed two problems: (1) our resolver order between tenant rollouts and client pins is ambiguous; (2) edge devices need a compact, signed manifest for offline pin resolution. We should handle both in the same RFC follow-up.
Devon: agree. We have several competing constraints: backward compatibility, deterministic resolution across replicas, and minimal console/SDK churn.
Priya: proposal sketch: introduce three orthogonal fields on client_pin: scope (route|app|tenant), pin_epoch (int), and pin_type (hard|soft). Add precedence (int) as optional. Resolver picks winner by: 1) highest scope specificity (route > app > tenant), 2) highest pin_epoch, 3) highest precedence, 4) tie-break by controller_id lexicographically.
Ana: sounds deterministic. For legacy client_pin we default to scope=tenant, pin_epoch=0, pin_type=soft, precedence=10. Document mapping.
Devon: for atomic transitions across pools add a prepare/commit handshake: control plane writes a pin with state=preparing + pin_epoch=N, waits for >= quorum readiness (pools load model and report), then flips state=active. If timeout, state=aborted and we rollback. This avoids clients seeing half-applied pins.
Priya: prepare will increase memory pressure since pools load both old and new models. Add optional grace_duration on the pin so pools keep old KV cache valid for X seconds after commit to smooth transitions.
Ana: for edge/offline we need a signed manifest format: manifest_id, issued_at, expires_at, pins[], compatibility_tags, signature. Support delta_base for compact diffs. Nodes apply highest manifest_version that is valid and signed. Signed manifests required for hard pins; soft pins can be unsigned but treated lower precedence when offline.
Devon: deterministic offline resolver rules: choose highest precedence pin that is unexpired and whose compatibility_tags are satisfied by local runtime. If none match, use manifest.provided fallback_hint or local default. Tie-breaking as above.
Priya: to avoid replay/old-manifest issues include manifest_nonce + revocation list. Nodes periodically fetch revocations when online and immediately reject revoked manifests. Also expose manifest lineage in console for auditing.
Ana: telemetry & observability: emit pin.transition.{prepare,ready,commit,abort} with tags {tenant,scope,route,pin_epoch,target_model,reason}. Resolver should optionally return a compact decision_trace in response headers when debug enabled: e.g. X-Resolver-Trace: winner=client_pin;scope=route;pin_epoch=7;reason=hard_pin_unavailable_fallback.
Devon: ops safety: rate-limit pin updates per-tenant (e.g., max 5 updates/min). Alert if pin_transition.abort rate > threshold. Also expose memory pressure gauges per-pool during prepares.
Priya: SDK/console notes: console shows per-scope pin UI with a "prepare" progress bar and expected memory delta. SDKs will surface pin_epoch, manifest_id (if any), and decision_trace header when debug flag set.
Ana: migration plan: Phase 1 accept new fields server-side and map legacy pins to defaults; Phase 2 add prepare state machine and manifest support behind feature flags; Phase 3 enable defaults (hard pins top priority + manifest enforcement) after 2-week notice and SDK bump.
Devon: tests: add replica-order fuzzing to ensure deterministic tie-break, chaos tests for partial model loads, and an offline-manifest apply/revoke test harness.
Priya: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with schema examples, the prepare/commit statechart, manifest delta spec, and telemetry table. Tagging owners: Devon -> resolver impl + tests, Ana -> console + migration docs, Priya -> RFC + telemetry.
cheng-bot: canary deploy queued: resolver-pin-prepare-v1 -> staging. ETA ~13m. :rocket:
Ana: thanks all. Drop any staging regressions back into this thread. :thumbsup:
